ai.description: Dendrelaphis tristis is a slender, arboreal snake reaching 1.5m. It features a bronze-brown back, a cream belly, and a distinct black eye-stripe. A white lateral line often borders the dark flank.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dendrelaphis tristis* is best distinguished by the prominent, thick black stripe running through the eye and along the neck, which fades into a series of dark spots posteriorly.
ai.habitat: Dendrelaphis tristis inhabits diverse environments, including moist deciduous forests, scrublands, and plantations, ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: Daudin's Bronzeback is a highly active, diurnal snake that hunts primarily in trees and shrubs, moving with remarkable speed and agility to capture its prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: Dendrelaphis tristis is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, often between June and October.
ai.distributionRemarks: Dendrelaphis tristis is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to Southern India, typically at elevations below 1,500m.
